dedupe_keys.name: ntsb investigation of the merrimack valley gas distribution overpressurization explosions and fires 13 september 2018

description: This case study is the National Transportation Safety Board investigation of the 13 September 2018 overpressurization of the Columbia Gas of Massachusetts distribution system in the Merrimack Valley, where high-pressure natural gas released into a low-pressure network caused a series of structure fires and explosions in Lawrence, Andover and North Andover. The events damaged 131 structures, destroyed at least 5 homes, left one person dead and two severely injured, mobilised fire departments under the Massachusetts fire mobilisation plan with mutual aid, led emergency officials to cut electrical power and close roads and rail, and forced the shutdown of the low-pressure system affecting 10,894 customers. The NTSB found the probable cause to be weak engineering management that did not adequately plan, review, sequence and oversee a construction project that abandoned a cast iron main without first relocating regulator sensing lines to the new polyethylene main, with a low-pressure system lacking adequate overpressure protection. Access: the page links the completed investigation, docket and recommendations P-18-005 to P-19-018 for free; no licence is stated. Caveats: an accident report, not a model or dataset. It suits emergency response and cascading failure scenario design and pipeline resilience policy, and relates to the San Bruno 2010 rupture case study catalogued here.
